title: Provenance of the four in-house descriptor rows of ATDrive Table 3A (US)
audit_verdict: No published method stands behind any of these four rows. They were designed inside this project. Every column is computed from the PDM-Lite reference rollout of the route (/data1/jeongtae/b2d_eval_sensors/route_<id>/anno/*.json.gz, 10 Hz), which is the same rollout the RelGraph encoder reads, so this is the protocol definition of a route representation and not leakage -- PDM-Lite is EXCLUDED_PLANNER and is not one of the 16 evaluated planners. But the rows must be described as PROBE-ROLLOUT descriptors, not as scene-only descriptors: the ego pose, the ego speed and the rollout length that enter them are PDM-Lite behaviour, and in three of the four sets a majority of the dimensions is either pure probe motion or an agent quantity measured in the probe frame.
how_scored: experiments/run_us.py:load_descriptor_arms -> two-stage Ridge plug-in: z-score on the calibration-type fold, Ridge(alpha = 100 if d > 10 else 10) fit b_hat ~ x, predict the evaluation types; pooled over 16 draws (640 route evaluations); AUROC / scene-MAE / Spearman rho.

columns.name: route_len
columns.formula: sum over valid frames of hypot(dx, dy) of the ego position
columns.input: anno['x'], anno['y'], anno['theta'], anno['speed'] (10 Hz; PDM-Lite reference rollout)

columns.name: n_wp
columns.formula: number of distinct consecutive near-target waypoints (|d(x,y)| > 1e-3) seen along the rollout
columns.input: anno['command_near'], anno['command_far'], anno['x_command_near'], anno['y_command_near'], anno['x_command_far'], anno['y_command_far']

columns.name: sum_turn
columns.formula: sum of |wrap(d heading)| between consecutive polyline segments of the unique near-target waypoints, segments shorter than 0.5 m dropped
columns.input: anno['command_near'], anno['command_far'], anno['x_command_near'], anno['y_command_near'], anno['x_command_far'], anno['y_command_far']

columns.name: max_turn
columns.formula: max of the same per-vertex |wrap(d heading)|
columns.input: anno['command_near'], anno['command_far'], anno['x_command_near'], anno['y_command_near'], anno['x_command_far'], anno['y_command_far']

columns.name: turn_per_m
columns.formula: sum_turn / max(route_len, 1.0)
columns.input: anno['x'], anno['y'], anno['theta'], anno['speed'] (10 Hz; PDM-Lite reference rollout) + anno['command_near'], anno['command_far'], anno['x_command_near'], anno['y_command_near'], anno['x_command_far'], anno['y_command_far']

columns.name: max_turn_20m
columns.formula: largest cumulative |d heading| inside any 20 m stretch of the waypoint polyline
columns.input: anno['command_near'], anno['command_far'], anno['x_command_near'], anno['y_command_near'], anno['x_command_far'], anno['y_command_far']

columns.name: n_cmd_seg
columns.formula: number of runs of constant command_near along the rollout frames
columns.input: anno['command_near'], anno['command_far'], anno['x_command_near'], anno['y_command_near'], anno['x_command_far'], anno['y_command_far']

columns.name: seg_per_100m
columns.formula: n_cmd_seg / max(route_len / 100, 1e-6)
columns.input: anno['x'], anno['y'], anno['theta'], anno['speed'] (10 Hz; PDM-Lite reference rollout) + anno['command_near'], anno['command_far'], anno['x_command_near'], anno['y_command_near'], anno['x_command_far'], anno['y_command_far']

columns.name: n_uniq_cmd
columns.formula: number of distinct command_near values in 1..6 over the rollout
columns.input: anno['command_near'], anno['command_far'], anno['x_command_near'], anno['y_command_near'], anno['x_command_far'], anno['y_command_far']

columns.name: lookahead_mean
columns.formula: mean over frames of the distance between the far and the near command target
columns.input: anno['command_near'], anno['command_far'], anno['x_command_near'], anno['y_command_near'], anno['x_command_far'], anno['y_command_far']

columns.name: distfrac_cmd1
columns.formula: ego travelled distance spent under command_near == 1, divided by the total travelled distance (distance-weighted, so a stopped probe adds nothing)
columns.input: anno['x'], anno['y'], anno['theta'], anno['speed'] (10 Hz; PDM-Lite reference rollout) + anno['command_near'], anno['command_far'], anno['x_command_near'], anno['y_command_near'], anno['x_command_far'], anno['y_command_far']

columns.input: anno['x'], anno['y'], anno['theta'], anno['speed'] (10 Hz; PDM-Lite reference rollout)

columns.input: anno['x'], anno['y'], anno['theta'], anno['speed'] (10 Hz; PDM-Lite reference rollout)

columns.name: n_agents_mean
columns.formula: mean over frames of the number of non-ego bounding boxes (no class filter, no radius filter)
columns.input: anno['bounding_boxes'][*]: class, location, rotation, extent, speed, lane_id, road_id (ego_vehicle entry excluded / used as the ego reference)

columns.name: n_agents_max
columns.formula: max over frames of the same count
columns.input: anno['bounding_boxes'][*]: class, location, rotation, extent, speed, lane_id, road_id (ego_vehicle entry excluded / used as the ego reference)

columns.name: n_near10_mean
columns.formula: mean over frames of the number of non-ego boxes within 10 m of the ego position
columns.input: anno['bounding_boxes'][*]: class, location, rotation, extent, speed, lane_id, road_id (ego_vehicle entry excluded / used as the ego reference) + anno['x'], anno['y'], anno['theta'], anno['speed'] (10 Hz; PDM-Lite reference rollout)

columns.name: n_near10_max
columns.formula: max over frames of the same count
columns.input: anno['bounding_boxes'][*]: class, location, rotation, extent, speed, lane_id, road_id (ego_vehicle entry excluded / used as the ego reference) + anno['x'], anno['y'], anno['theta'], anno['speed'] (10 Hz; PDM-Lite reference rollout)

columns.name: n_walker_mean
columns.formula: mean over frames of the number of boxes with class == 'walker'
columns.input: anno['bounding_boxes'][*]: class, location, rotation, extent, speed, lane_id, road_id (ego_vehicle entry excluded / used as the ego reference)

columns.name: frac_frames_with_walker
columns.formula: fraction of frames with at least one walker box
columns.input: anno['bounding_boxes'][*]: class, location, rotation, extent, speed, lane_id, road_id (ego_vehicle entry excluded / used as the ego reference)

columns.name: relspeed_mean
columns.formula: mean over frames of the per-frame mean of |agent speed - ego speed| over all non-ego boxes
columns.input: anno['bounding_boxes'][*]: class, location, rotation, extent, speed, lane_id, road_id (ego_vehicle entry excluded / used as the ego reference) + anno['x'], anno['y'], anno['theta'], anno['speed'] (10 Hz; PDM-Lite reference rollout)

columns.name: relspeed_max
columns.formula: max over frames of the per-frame max of |agent speed - ego speed|
columns.input: anno['bounding_boxes'][*]: class, location, rotation, extent, speed, lane_id, road_id (ego_vehicle entry excluded / used as the ego reference) + anno['x'], anno['y'], anno['theta'], anno['speed'] (10 Hz; PDM-Lite reference rollout)

notes: the heading used by dheading_mean/max comes from the ego position increments (atan2 of diff x, diff y), not from the logged theta, so it is undefined-noisy while the probe is stopped
no frame-validity mask is applied: every annotated frame of the rollout is used, and routes with fewer than 5 annotation files are skipped entirely by the producer
duration_s is the rollout length, i.e. it encodes how long PDM-Lite needed / how early the route terminated -- the most explicitly probe-dependent column of the set

Kinematics (cmdkin, 25d).producer: ORIGINAL PRODUCER MISSING from every repo; reconstructed at experiments/us_official/cmdkin.py:cmdkin and verified bit-for-bit (all 220 x 25 float32 values equal) against the shipped npz, recomputed from the raw anno
Kinematics (cmdkin, 25d).producer_status: reconstructed 2026-09; the two surviving slices (eval_cmdkin_kinonly.npz = cols 0:12, eval_cmdkin_cmdonly.npz = cols 12:25) are cut from this file by b2d_irt/scripts/cmdkin_decompose.py

reconstruction.numeric_detail: all statistics are evaluated on the float32 ego/cmd arrays produced by the eval_pipeline.load_anno cast; heading differences are wrapped with the float32 modulo form ((dh + pi) %% (2 pi) - pi). Any other wrap (np.angle(exp(i dh)), np.unwrap, arctan2, or the same modulo in float64) reproduces yaw_mean / yaw_max only to about 1.8e-07, i.e. not bit-for-bit; computing the whole block in float64 breaks 9 of the 25 columns at the float32 ULP level.
reconstruction.scored: AUROC 0.7519106345648979 / scene-MAE 0.18029126621966515 / rho 0.49723177046454564 -- identical to 16 digits to the shipped "Kinematics (cmdkin)" row (experiments/us_official/score_one.py).

Kinematics (cmdkin, 25d).verified: all 220 x 25 float32 values regenerated from the raw anno by experiments/us_official/cmdkin.py are bit-for-bit identical to the shipped npz, and the rebuilt file scores identically to 16 digits in Table 3A.

columns.name: gtrisk_mean_inv_ttc_vr
columns.formula: plain mean over the sub-sampled time steps (every 5th frame, 2 Hz) of the per-step channel: 1 / max(min_agent TTC, 0.5) with TTC the first root of the elliptical-footprint overlap under constant velocity, ego driving straight at its realized speed; footprint semi-axes (ego half-length + agent half-length + 0.3 m) x (ego half-width + agent half-width + 0.3 m); TTC = 0 when already overlapping
columns.input: anno['bounding_boxes'][*]: class, location, rotation, extent, speed, lane_id, road_id (ego_vehicle entry excluded / used as the ego reference) + anno['x'], anno['y'], anno['theta'], anno['speed'] (10 Hz; PDM-Lite reference rollout)

columns.name: gtrisk_mean_rdec_vr
columns.formula: plain mean over the sub-sampled time steps (every 5th frame, 2 Hz) of the per-step channel: max over agents inside the ego corridor (|y_ego-frame| < B and x > 0) of dv^2 / (2 gap), dv = ego realized speed - agent longitudinal speed, gap = max(x - A, 0.5)
columns.input: anno['bounding_boxes'][*]: class, location, rotation, extent, speed, lane_id, road_id (ego_vehicle entry excluded / used as the ego reference) + anno['x'], anno['y'], anno['theta'], anno['speed'] (10 Hz; PDM-Lite reference rollout)

columns.name: gtrisk_mean_n_conflict_vr
columns.formula: plain mean over the sub-sampled time steps (every 5th frame, 2 Hz) of the per-step channel: number of agents whose constant-velocity closest approach within a 4 s horizon lands inside the inflated ego footprint (normalized elliptical distance < 1), ego at its realized speed
columns.input: anno['bounding_boxes'][*]: class, location, rotation, extent, speed, lane_id, road_id (ego_vehicle entry excluded / used as the ego reference) + anno['x'], anno['y'], anno['theta'], anno['speed'] (10 Hz; PDM-Lite reference rollout)

columns.name: gtrisk_mean_inv_ttc_v0
columns.formula: plain mean over the sub-sampled time steps (every 5th frame, 2 Hz) of the per-step channel: same as inv_ttc_vr with the ego speed replaced by V0 = 8 m/s
columns.input: anno['bounding_boxes'][*]: class, location, rotation, extent, speed, lane_id, road_id (ego_vehicle entry excluded / used as the ego reference) + anno['x'], anno['y'], anno['theta'], anno['speed'] (10 Hz; PDM-Lite reference rollout)

source_taxonomy.probe_ego_motion: PDM-Lite's own recorded ego pose / speed only
source_taxonomy.probe_route_command: the route command + nav-target channel logged frame by frame along the PDM-Lite rollout (route definition, but truncated / resampled by where and how long the probe actually drove)
source_taxonomy.probe_ego_x_command: a ratio or weighting that mixes PDM-Lite's travelled distance with the route command channel
source_taxonomy.other_agents: other agents only (counts over all logged boxes; no ego reference)
source_taxonomy.other_agents_at_probe_pose: other agents evaluated in PDM-Lite's rollout ego frame (pose/heading), but not using the ego speed
source_taxonomy.other_agents_at_probe_pose_and_speed: other agents evaluated at PDM-Lite's rollout pose AND its realized speed
source_taxonomy.other_agents_at_probe_pose_counterfactua: other agents evaluated at PDM-Lite's rollout pose with the ego speed replaced by a nominal 8 m/s

probe_vs_scene_accounting.question: per set, how many dimensions come from PDM-Lite own ego motion versus the surrounding scene

Route geometry (16d).reading: all 16 dimensions are read off the PDM-Lite rollout log; zero dimensions see any other agent. The 7 "route command" dimensions describe the nav route rather than the probe motion, but they are still rollout-conditioned (the waypoint polyline only extends as far as PDM-Lite drove, and n_cmd_seg counts frames).

Agent density + kin. (18d).reading: 10 of 18 are pure probe motion (including duration_s, which is literally how long PDM-Lite took). Of the 8 scene dimensions only 4 (n_agents_mean/max, n_walker_mean, frac_frames_with_walker) are ego-independent; the other 4 are measured relative to the probe pose (10 m radius) or its speed.

Kinematics (cmdkin, 25d).reading: all 25 dimensions come from the PDM-Lite rollout and none sees another agent. The 13 command dimensions are TIME-weighted fractions, so probe dwell time (55% of the eval steps are a stopped probe) enters them directly.

Hand-crafted risk (cmdkin+gtrisk, 73d).reading: 25 of 73 are the probe-only cmdkin block. All 48 gtrisk dimensions involve other agents but every one of them is evaluated in the probe rollout ego frame; 9 also use the probe realized speed and 9 replace it with 8 m/s. Zero dimensions are independent of the probe.

probe_vs_scene_accounting.paper_wording: these four rows are probe-rollout descriptors, not scene-only descriptors

ssm_conformance.reference: B. Westhofen, C. Neurohr, T. Koopmann, M. Butz, B. Boede, F. Reichenbaecher, M. Bollmann, R. Schuldes, J. Hoffmann, "Criticality Metrics for Automated Driving: A Review and Suitability Analysis of the Available Metrics", arXiv:2108.02403 (Artificial Intelligence Review, 2023); TTC/DRAC/PET definitions in the time-scale and deceleration-scale metric sections.
ssm_conformance.scope: the surrogate-safety columns of the gtrisk block only (b2d_irt/scripts/gt_risk.py:step_risk / step_static)

inv_ttc_vr.why: It is a legitimate 2D constant-velocity TTC: first positive root of the relative-motion overlap of two inflated elliptical footprints, minimised over agents. Deviations from the standard definition: (a) the ego is propagated STRAIGHT along its current heading, its yaw rate is ignored, so TTC is wrong on exactly the turning conflicts the bank is full of; (b) footprints are ellipses inflated by 0.3 m rather than rectangles, which makes overlap optimistic at the corners; (c) the value stored is 1 / max(TTC, 0.5 s), a monotone but saturating transform, so every conflict below 0.5 s is indistinguishable (cap 2.0); (d) already-overlapping agents get TTC = 0 -> the cap value.

inv_ttc_v0.why: the ego speed is replaced by a nominal 8 m/s, so it is not the TTC of the observed scene but of a counterfactual constant-speed ego on the probe path. It is a what-if criticality index, not a surrogate safety measure of the log.

rdec_vr.claimed: DRAC (deceleration rate to avoid a crash)
rdec_vr.why: the formula dv^2 / (2 gap) is exactly the standard DRAC. Caveats: the leader set is chosen by a rectangular corridor test in the ego frame (|lateral| < combined half-width + 0.3 m, longitudinal > 0) rather than by lane assignment, and the gap is floored at 0.5 m so DRAC saturates instead of diverging on contact; the scene value is the max over in-corridor agents (a scene-level aggregation of a pairwise metric, which is standard practice).

rdec_v0.why: same counterfactual 8 m/s ego speed as inv_ttc_v0; DRAC is defined on the observed closing speed.

n_conflict_vr / n_conflict_v0.why: counts agents whose constant-velocity closest approach inside a 4 s horizon falls inside the inflated ego footprint. This is a thresholded distance-of-closest-approach / predicted-minimum-distance quantity, not TTC, DRAC or PET. Reporting it as "conflicts" is fine as long as the paper does not call it an SSM.

inv_gap.why: inverse minimum surface-to-surface distance; a distance-scale proximity index, not one of the named SSMs.

closing_max.why: positive range rate towards a STATIONARY ego. It is a legitimate probe-free approach-rate channel but it is not TTC (no size, no collision condition).

PET.why: no post-encroachment time is computed anywhere in gtrisk. PET requires the times at which two road users successively occupy a shared conflict area, which needs a conflict-area definition and no motion prediction; the gtrisk conflict channels are prediction-based instead. If the paper text claims a PET baseline, that claim is unsupported by this feature file.

ssm_conformance.summary: Of the standard trio, DRAC is implemented conformantly (in the _vr variant), TTC is implemented as a straight-line constant-velocity 2D approximation with a 0.5 s floor and an inverted scale, and PET is absent. The _v0 duplicates of TTC and DRAC are counterfactual and should not be described as surrogate safety measures of the recorded scene.

known_defects_inherited_from_the_produce: gt_risk.py's own layout string records that the '_v0 is probe-free' claim was refuted on review: the ego POSE is still the probe rollout pose (about 55% of eval steps are a stopped probe), and the 39-d "probe-free" subset falls to rho +0.072 after residualising on cmdkin.
cmdkin_decompose.py documents that the cmdkin command block is TIME-weighted, so a probe that dwells inflates whichever command it was in; that is why the distance-weighted routegeom arm exists.

baseline_kin_den den channels apply no class filter and no radius filter to the bounding boxes; in the 220 eval routes the only classes present are vehicle / walker / ego_vehicle, so the count is effectively "all vehicles and walkers logged in the frame", however far away.
